summary: Tennis for Two entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Tennis for Two
entries.definitive_edition: Original Brookhaven hardware design, with recreation clearly labeled

emulation.emulator: Museum recreation or custom simulation only
emulation.notes: Original analog hardware behavior is the reference point.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Brookhaven-style hardware recreation based on documented original design

primary.version: Original 1958 Tennis for Two hardware design
primary.why: Tennis for Two was an analog-computer/oscilloscope exhibition game at Brookhaven National Laboratory, not a commercial software release. The authentic archive route is the original hardware design or Brookhaven-style recreation/documentation.
primary.how_to_play: Archive as a historical hardware exhibit. Record whether using original documentation, Brookhaven recreation footage, museum emulation, controller design, oscilloscope/display behavior, and gravity/settings variant if the 1959 version is shown.

all_releases.fidelity: Original analog computer, oscilloscope, and custom-controller exhibit.
Historical larger-screen/enhanced exhibit with additional gravity behavior.
all_releases.reason: secondary: document as the second-year historical variant if source material is available.

all_releases.fidelity: Practical modern recreations and museum emulations.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful access route, but must be labeled as recreation rather than original release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The original hardware was dismantled, so current play depends on reconstructions, emulations, or documentation rather than a distributed build.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat modern tennis clones as Tennis for Two. Record recreation/emulation provenance.
